Having the right vehicle, booked in advance and driven by someone who understands how to secure a chair properly, makes those many trips across the city much less stressful.

Taxi Peninsula’s wheelchair accessible vans and Maxi WAT are built for this. The Maxi WAT’s hydraulic hoist handles heavier power chairs, and every wheelchair vehicle has four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts. Carers travel with the passenger, and we offer fixed quotes for the long trip from the Peninsula. NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted.

faq.q: Can you transport someone with a spinal injury in their power chair?
faq.a: Yes. Book the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist suitable for heavier power chairs and carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. The chair is secured with four-point restraints and the passenger wears a lap-sash seatbelt. Let us know the chair type and any special requirements in your booking notes.

faq.q: Is it practical to take a taxi from the Peninsula to Heidelberg?
faq.a: Yes. It is a long trip across Melbourne, but door-to-door travel is much easier than several train and bus connections. We show a fare estimate before you book and offer fixed quotes on request. NDIS and aged-care accounts can be used where your plan or package covers transport.

name: Box Hill Hospital
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi from the Peninsula to Box Hill Hospital for appointments, visits and discharge. Door-to-door help, 24/7.
entrance: Box Hill Hospital has a main entrance on Arnold Street with step-free access. Tell us your clinic or ward so the driver can choose the best entrance.
spot: We drop off at the main entrance set-down area. If you are going to the emergency department, tell us so we head straight there.
parking: Parking around the hospital and Box Hill’s busy centre is limited. A drop-off saves time, especially at peak visiting hours.
access: The main building has step-free access and lifts. Drivers are happy to push a manual chair or carry bags to the door.
tips: Add your clinic or ward name to the booking notes.
Traffic around Box Hill’s centre can be slow; allow extra time.
Ask for a fixed quote for the trip from the Peninsula.
pickup: Patients usually meet the taxi at the main entrance on Arnold Street. We will call or message when we arrive.
about: Box Hill Hospital is a major public hospital in Melbourne’s east, run by Eastern Health. It has an emergency department, a wide range of medical and surgical services and specialist clinics, serving a large population across the eastern suburbs.

Peninsula residents usually come to Box Hill to visit family who live in the east, or because a relative has been admitted there. Some are referred to specialist clinics on the site. It is a long trip from Frankston or the Peninsula, and without a car it involves several changes on public transport. When a parent who lives in the eastern suburbs is admitted, adult children from the Peninsula may need to make the trip many times over a short period. Some patients are also discharged from Box Hill to stay with family on the Peninsula while they recover, which means a long ride home with bags, medication and perhaps a new walking aid. We can handle all of those trips.

Taxi Peninsula provides direct, door-to-door trips from anywhere on the Peninsula to Box Hill Hospital. Choose a sedan or a wheelchair accessible vehicle, bring a carer along, and get a fare estimate or fixed quote before you travel. We run 24 hours, every day.

faq.q: Can you take me from Frankston to visit a relative at Box Hill Hospital?
faq.a: Yes. Book online with Box Hill Hospital as your destination, and choose a return pick-up time or “pick up when ready” for the trip home. Fare estimates are shown before you confirm, and fixed quotes are available on request for this longer trip across Melbourne.

faq.q: Can you bring a patient from Box Hill Hospital to the Peninsula after discharge?
faq.a: Yes. Book a “pick up when ready” trip from Box Hill Hospital to their home on the Peninsula. Choose a wheelchair accessible vehicle if they are leaving in a wheelchair. A carer can travel with them, and our driver will help them to the door at home.

name: The Alfred
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi from the Peninsula to The Alfred on Commercial Road for clinics, surgery, visits and discharge. Book 24/7.
entrance: The Alfred has a main entrance on Commercial Road and several other entrances around the site. Tell us your department and we will aim for the nearest step-free door.
spot: We drop off at the main Commercial Road set-down area, or closer to your clinic where the site allows.
parking: Parking at The Alfred is in high demand and street parking nearby is restricted. Being dropped at the door is quicker and less stressful.
access: Entrances at The Alfred are step-free, with lifts to all wards. Our drivers can carry bags and help you to the entrance.
tips: Add your department, clinic or ward to the booking notes.
Commercial Road and St Kilda Road are busy at peak times; allow extra time.
If a relative is being discharged, use “pick up when ready”.
Patients moving on to Caulfield Hospital for rehab can book us for later visiting trips.
pickup: Patients usually meet the taxi at the main entrance on Commercial Road. Tell us your ward and we will confirm by SMS or phone.
about: The Alfred is a major public teaching hospital in Melbourne, run by Alfred Health. It is home to one of Victoria’s major trauma centres and the statewide adult burns service, along with heart and lung transplant services and a broad range of other specialties.

Peninsula residents are often taken to The Alfred after a serious accident, or referred for specialist care. Family members may need to visit for weeks, and patients may return regularly for follow-up clinics after going home. The drive up the Nepean Highway and into the city, with limited parking at the end, is draining when you are already worried about a loved one. Patients transferred to Caulfield Hospital for rehabilitation, or discharged home with ongoing care, often need several trips back for clinics and reviews.

Taxi Peninsula takes you directly from home to The Alfred’s entrance. Choose a sedan, a wheelchair accessible van or a Maxi WAT, travel with a carer, and book a return at a set time or when you are ready. Fixed quotes are available on request, and NDIS and aged-care accounts and MPTP cards are accepted.

faq.q: A family member was taken to The Alfred after an accident. Can you get us there?
faq.a: Yes. We run 24 hours, so we can bring family members up from the Peninsula day or night, though booking ahead is recommended when possible. Several people can travel together, and our Maxi WAT seats up to six plus two wheelchairs if you need a larger vehicle.

faq.q: Can I book regular trips for follow-up clinics at The Alfred?
faq.a: Yes. Book each appointment online, or call us to set up several bookings at once. Add the clinic name to the notes so the driver drops you at the right entrance. For the trip home, “pick up when ready” helps when clinic times run over.

name: Melbourne Airport
description: Taxi and maxi taxi between the Mornington Peninsula and Melbourne Airport. Flight tracking, early starts, luggage help, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: Each terminal has step-free access from the forecourt into check-in and arrivals, with lifts and ramps between levels. Tell us your airline so we head to the right terminal.
spot: For departures we drop you at your terminal’s departures forecourt. For arrivals, we confirm the pick-up area by SMS or phone, as airport pick-up zones are separate from the terminal doors and can change.
parking: Waiting at the kerb is not permitted, so drivers wait in the designated area until you have collected your bags. Adding your flight number lets us time this around your actual landing.
access: Terminals have lifts, accessible toilets and assistance available through your airline. If you need wheelchair assistance inside the terminal, arrange it with your airline when you book your flight.
tips: Add your flight number when booking so we track delays and early arrivals.
Tell us your airline and whether the flight is domestic or international; international flights use Terminal 2.
Groups and families with lots of luggage should book the Maxi WAT.
Book early-morning departures the day before, with time for check-in and security.
about: Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine is the city’s main airport, handling both international flights and the majority of domestic services. It has four terminals, with international flights operating from Terminal 2 and domestic flights spread across the other terminals by airline.

For people on the Mornington Peninsula and in Frankston, Tullamarine is on the far side of Melbourne, and getting there with luggage before a dawn flight is a real hassle. Long-term parking adds up over a holiday, and asking a friend to drive across the city at 4am is a big favour. Coming home after a long-haul flight, few people feel like driving. Families heading away for school holidays also need room for suitcases, prams and car seats.

Taxi Peninsula runs airport transfers 24 hours a day. Add your flight number and we track your flight, so your driver is ready when you land, even if you are early or delayed. Our drivers help with bags, sedans suit couples and solo travellers, and the Maxi WAT carries larger groups or wheelchair users with their luggage. You will see a fare estimate when booking, and fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: What happens if my flight into Melbourne Airport is delayed?
faq.a: Add your flight number when you book and we track your flight. If it lands late, your pick-up moves with it, and if it lands early, we adjust where possible. Once you have your bags, call or reply to your confirmation and we will direct you to the driver in the airport pick-up area.

faq.q: Can you take a family with lots of luggage to the airport?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us how many people are travelling and how much luggage you have. A sedan suits smaller groups, while our Maxi WAT carries up to six seated passengers plus luggage, or wheelchairs and their users. Drivers load and unload your bags at both ends.

name: Avalon Airport
description: Taxi from the Mornington Peninsula and Frankston to Avalon Airport near Geelong. Flight tracking, luggage help, maxi for groups, 24/7.
entrance: Avalon has a single, compact terminal with step-free access from the forecourt into check-in and arrivals.
spot: We drop you right at the terminal’s departure area. For arrivals, we will confirm the pick-up spot when you land, as it is separate from the terminal door.
parking: The terminal is small, so walking distances are short. Drivers wait in the permitted pick-up area, and we track your flight so waiting is kept to a minimum.
access: The terminal is compact, which keeps walking short for travellers with limited mobility. Arrange any assistance at the gate directly with your airline.
tips: Check whether your flight departs from Avalon or Melbourne Airport; it is easy to mix them up.
Add your flight number so we can track your arrival.
Avalon is between Melbourne and Geelong, so allow plenty of time for the trip around the bay.
Ask for a fixed quote if you prefer a set price for the longer trip.
about: Avalon Airport is a smaller airport between Melbourne and Geelong, near the town of Lara. It handles a limited number of domestic flights, mostly with low-cost airlines, and is popular with travellers from Geelong and the west who want a quicker, simpler terminal experience.

For Peninsula residents, Avalon sometimes offers a cheaper fare or a better flight time, but it is a long way around the bay by road. Public transport options to the airport are limited, especially for early or late flights, and parking for several days adds to the cost of the trip. From the Peninsula, the route runs around the top of the bay and through the western suburbs, so the drive takes some planning, particularly for an early departure. Coming home late in the evening, a booked ride waiting at the terminal is much easier than finding your car in a dark car park and making the long drive back to the Peninsula yourself.

Taxi Peninsula can take you to Avalon from anywhere on the Peninsula or in Frankston, at any hour. Add your flight number for the trip home and we will track your landing. Sedans suit most travellers, and the Maxi WAT takes groups, wheelchair users and bulky luggage. Fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: Is Avalon Airport the same as Melbourne Airport?
faq.a: No. Avalon is a separate airport between Melbourne and Geelong, while Melbourne Airport is at Tullamarine in the north-west. Check your booking confirmation to see which one your flight uses, and enter the correct airport when you book your taxi so we plan the right route and timing.

faq.q: Can you pick me up from Avalon Airport late at night?
faq.a: Yes. We run 24 hours a day. Add your flight number to the booking and we track your flight, so the driver is there when you land, even if your flight is delayed. Once you have your bags, call us or reply to your confirmation and we will direct you to the driver.

name: Moorabbin Airport
description: Taxi to Moorabbin Airport for flight lessons, charter flights and aviation work. Easy trips from Frankston and the Peninsula, 24/7.
entrance: Moorabbin Airport is spread out, with many separate buildings, hangars and flying schools rather than a single terminal. Tell us the business or building you are heading to.
spot: We drop you at the address of your flying school, charter operator or business. A street number or business name in your booking notes is essential.
parking: Parking is generally available near the businesses on site, but a taxi is handy if you are leaving a car elsewhere or flying out on a charter.
access: Access varies building by building. Let us know if you need a step-free entrance and we will help you find the closest door.
tips: Give us the exact business name or street address on the airport site, not just “Moorabbin Airport”.
If you are flying out on a charter, tell us the departure time so we allow enough time.
Student pilots can book regular trips to lessons.
about: Moorabbin Airport is a busy general aviation airport in Melbourne’s south-east. It is known for flight training, with many flying schools on site, along with charter operators, aircraft maintenance businesses and other aviation services.

People from Frankston and the Peninsula travel to Moorabbin Airport for flying lessons, charter or private flights, and work at the many aviation businesses on the site. Others visit for business meetings or to collect someone arriving on a private flight. Without a single terminal, it is easy for a first-time visitor to end up at the wrong building. Student pilots in particular often have early lessons and may be too young to drive or not have a car. Charter passengers and people collecting aircraft also need a reliable way to reach a specific hangar on time, particularly when flights are timed around weather and daylight.

Taxi Peninsula takes you directly to the business or building you need. Add the exact address or business name to your booking, and our driver will find the right entrance. Sedans suit most trips, and we can send a wheelchair accessible vehicle where needed. We run 24 hours, so early lessons and late returns are not a problem.

faq.q: Moorabbin Airport doesn’t have one terminal. Where will you drop me?
faq.a: We drop you at the specific business or building you tell us. Include the flying school, charter company or street address in your booking notes, and the driver will take you there. If you are being picked up, tell us the same details so the driver can find you quickly.

faq.q: Can you take me to regular flying lessons?
faq.a: Yes. Many student pilots need reliable transport for early lessons or when they cannot drive. Book each trip online, or call us to arrange several bookings. Remember that lessons may be cancelled due to weather, so update or cancel your booking if your instructor reschedules.

name: Essendon Fields Airport
description: Taxi from the Peninsula to Essendon Fields Airport for charter, business jet and regional flights. Flight tracking, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: Different operators at Essendon Fields use different terminal buildings. Tell us your operator and we will take you to the right entrance.
spot: We drop you at your operator’s terminal or building. The operator’s name and any address details on your itinerary help the driver.
parking: Parking is available on the airport precinct, but a taxi avoids leaving a car for the length of your trip.
access: Access depends on the operator’s building. Let us know if you need a step-free entrance and we will help you find it.
tips: Bring your operator’s name and departure details when you book.
Add your flight number or tail number for pick-ups if you have one.
Allow for traffic across the city, particularly on the freeways at peak times.
about: Essendon Fields Airport is in Melbourne’s north-west, close to Essendon and Strathmore. Once Melbourne’s main airport, it now handles mainly business and private aviation, charter flights, and some regional services.

Peninsula residents fly from Essendon Fields for charter flights, business trips, regional connections and private flights. It is a long trip across the city from Frankston or the Mornington Peninsula, and charter departures are often early in the morning. Business travellers heading to meetings interstate often fly from here to save time, and regional services attract passengers who prefer its smaller scale. Without a car, getting there from the south-east involves a train into the city and another connection out again, which is impractical for an early departure with luggage. A direct taxi is far simpler, and you can be dropped at your operator’s door.

Taxi Peninsula provides 24-hour transfers between your home and Essendon Fields. We drop you at your operator’s building, help with luggage, and track your flight for return pick-ups where possible. Choose a sedan or, for larger groups or wheelchair users, our Maxi WAT. Fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: Is Essendon Fields the same as Melbourne Airport?
faq.a: No. Essendon Fields is a separate airport closer to the city, used mainly for business jets, charter and some regional flights. Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine handles most commercial flights. Check your itinerary and enter the correct airport when you book.

faq.q: Can you meet me after a charter flight into Essendon Fields?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up and include your operator’s name and expected arrival time, plus a flight number if you have one. We will confirm the meeting point by SMS or phone once you land, and the driver will help with your bags and take you straight home to the Peninsula.

name: Searoad Ferries Sorrento
description: Taxi to the Searoad Ferries terminal in Sorrento for the crossing to Queenscliff. Luggage help and wheelchair taxis, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: The Searoad terminal at Sorrento has step-free access for foot passengers. Our driver will drop you as close as the terminal’s set-down area allows.
spot: We drop off outside the terminal, where foot passengers can walk straight in. Tell us if you have bikes, prams or a lot of luggage.
parking: The terminal car park and Sorrento streets are very busy in summer. Being dropped off avoids leaving a car for the day.
access: Foot passenger access to the terminal and ferry is generally step-free. Check with Searoad if you need assistance boarding with a wheelchair.
tips: Check Searoad’s timetable before booking and allow time to buy your ticket.
Summer weekends and school holidays are busy; book your taxi ahead.
If you are going on to Geelong or Torquay, arrange onward transport from Queenscliff before you cross.
Tell us if you have a wheelchair so we send a wheelchair accessible vehicle.
about: Searoad Ferries runs the car and passenger ferry across the mouth of Port Phillip between Sorrento and Queenscliff. The crossing links the Mornington Peninsula with the Bellarine Peninsula, Geelong and the Great Ocean Road, and is a popular day trip in its own right, with views of the heads and sometimes dolphins.

Many people cross as foot passengers, whether they are visiting Queenscliff for the day, connecting to Geelong or heading further west. Others are holidaymakers staying in Sorrento, Rye or Blairgowrie who want to see the Bellarine without bringing their car. Getting to the terminal without driving is easy with a taxi, particularly in summer when parking is scarce. Groups of friends, cyclists and families with young children all use the ferry, and getting everyone to the terminal on time is easier when nobody has to worry about where to leave the car.

Taxi Peninsula can take you to the Sorrento terminal from anywhere on the Peninsula, and pick you up again when you return. Our drivers help with luggage, and our wheelchair accessible vehicles carry passengers in their chairs. Check the ferry timetable, choose a pick-up time with plenty of leeway, and book online or by phone.

faq.q: Can you pick me up when I come back on the ferry?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up from the Searoad terminal in Sorrento for the time your return ferry is due. If you are not sure which crossing you will catch, choose “pick up when ready” and call us or tap “I’m ready” once you know. The driver will meet you near the terminal.

faq.q: How early should I arrive for the ferry?
faq.a: Check Searoad Ferries’ own advice for foot passengers, as it can vary with the season. As a general rule, allow time to buy a ticket and walk on, and give yourself extra leeway on summer weekends when traffic around Sorrento is slow. We will plan your pick-up time accordingly.

name: Stony Point Ferry Terminal
description: Taxi to Stony Point Ferry Terminal for ferries to French Island and Phillip Island. Luggage help, wheelchair taxis, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: The terminal is at the end of the Stony Point jetty area. Access to the waiting area is generally level, though the pier and gangways can vary with the tide.
spot: We drop you near the ferry terminal entrance, as close to the jetty as vehicles are allowed. Tell us if you have bikes or bulky luggage.
parking: Parking is available near the terminal, but a taxi saves leaving a car behind while you are on the islands.
access: Boarding can involve ramps or gangways that vary with tides. If you use a wheelchair, check with the ferry operator about boarding before you travel.
tips: Check the ferry timetable before booking your taxi.
If you are staying on French Island or Phillip Island, book your return pick-up in advance.
Bring a jacket, as the jetty can be windy and cold.
about: Stony Point Ferry Terminal is on Western Port, at the end of the road through Crib Point. Passenger ferries run from here to Tankerton on French Island and to Cowes on Phillip Island, making Stony Point the main gateway between the Mornington Peninsula and the Western Port islands.

People catch the ferry for day trips to French Island’s walking and cycling tracks, for visits to Cowes, or to commute to work on the islands. The terminal sits next to Stony Point railway station, but trains on this line are infrequent, so many travellers prefer a direct taxi. French Island has very limited roads and services, so visitors often travel light and on foot or by bike. Residents of the islands also cross to the mainland for appointments, shopping and to connect with trains, and need a reliable ride from the jetty to wherever they are going on the Peninsula or in Frankston.

Taxi Peninsula takes you to Stony Point from anywhere on the Peninsula or in Frankston, with help for luggage and bikes. Our wheelchair accessible vehicles carry passengers in their chairs, and you can book a return pick-up for when your ferry comes back. Check the timetable, then book online or call us.

faq.q: Can you meet me when the ferry comes back to Stony Point?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up from Stony Point for the time your return ferry is due. If plans change, use “pick up when ready” and call us or tap “I’m ready” when you know your arrival time. The driver will wait near the terminal entrance.

faq.q: Can I bring my bike in the taxi?
faq.a: Tell us when you book. A bike may fit in a sedan depending on its size, but a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT has more room. Our drivers will help load and unload, and we will make sure it is secured for the trip.

name: Station Pier (Port Melbourne)
description: Taxi from the Peninsula to Station Pier in Port Melbourne for cruise ship departures. Luggage help, maxi for groups, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: Station Pier has a passenger terminal with step-free access. On cruise days, the cruise line and port set up specific drop-off and check-in arrangements.
spot: We drop you in the area set aside for cruise passengers on embarkation day. Follow signs and staff instructions to check-in.
parking: Parking near Station Pier is limited on cruise days. A taxi saves parking a car for the length of your cruise.
access: The terminal is step-free. If you need wheelchair assistance boarding, arrange it through your cruise line in advance.
tips: Check your cruise line’s check-in time and book your taxi to arrive within your allotted window.
Spirit of Tasmania now departs from Geelong, not Station Pier; check where your ship leaves from.
Families with lots of luggage should book the Maxi WAT.
For your return, book a pick-up for the morning your ship docks, and confirm the time once you are back in port.
about: Station Pier in Port Melbourne is Melbourne’s main cruise ship terminal. During the cruise season, large ships call here regularly, both for round trips from Melbourne and as a port of call on longer voyages.

Peninsula residents heading off on a cruise need to get themselves and their luggage to Port Melbourne for a set check-in window. Parking near the pier is limited and costly for the length of a cruise, and it is a long drive home after disembarking. Cruise passengers often travel with large suitcases and need to arrive within a specific check-in window, which makes timing important. On busy days, more than one ship can be in port and the roads around the pier get congested. Coming home, passengers disembark early in the morning and often face a long wait for other transport. For groups of friends or extended families cruising together, a single larger vehicle keeps everyone and their luggage together.

Taxi Peninsula provides direct transfers to and from Station Pier. Our drivers help with bags, sedans suit couples, and our Maxi WAT takes groups and wheelchair users with luggage. Book ahead for embarkation day, and book a pick-up for when your ship returns. Fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: When should I book my taxi to Station Pier?
faq.a: Check your cruise documents for your check-in time and book a pick-up that gets you there within that window, allowing for traffic. Book a few days ahead, as cruise days are busy. Add any special requirements, such as a wheelchair or lots of luggage, in your booking notes.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from Station Pier when our cruise ends?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up for the day your ship returns, and use “pick up when ready” if you are not sure what time you will disembark. Once you have collected your luggage, call us or tap “I’m ready” and we will direct you to the driver.

name: Frankston Station
description: Taxi pick-ups from Frankston Station to anywhere on the Mornington Peninsula. Wheelchair taxis available, 24/7, book ahead or on arrival.
entrance: Frankston Station has step-free access between the platforms, concourse and street, with a bus interchange alongside.
spot: We meet you at a permitted pick-up point beside the station. The driver will confirm the exact spot by SMS or phone when they arrive.
parking: Stopping directly outside the station is restricted, and the bus interchange is for buses only. Drivers wait in a legal pick-up area and call you when they are there.
access: The station is accessible with ramps and lifts. If you are travelling with a wheelchair, book a wheelchair accessible taxi so we can meet you as you come off the train.
tips: Book ahead if your train arrives late at night, so the taxi is waiting.
Tell us which train you are on, so the driver can allow for delays.
Connections to the Stony Point line are at Frankston; let us know if you have missed one and want a taxi instead.
Use the station name and our pick-up confirmation to find the driver quickly.
about: Frankston Station is the end of the Frankston line and the main rail gateway to the Mornington Peninsula. It was rebuilt with a modern station building and bus interchange, and it is also where passengers change for the diesel shuttle to Stony Point.

Many people heading to the Peninsula arrive at Frankston by train and then need to get to Mornington, Mount Martha, Rosebud, Sorrento or the hinterland. Bus connections exist, but they can be slow or infrequent, especially at night and on weekends, and they are hard work with luggage or a wheelchair. Late at night, waiting for a bus after a train trip can be uncomfortable, and many passengers prefer to have a taxi booked and waiting. Others arrive with luggage after flying into Melbourne, or with a wheelchair or mobility aid, and need a vehicle that can take them directly to their door. Weekend visitors heading to the wineries or beaches also use the station as their starting point.

Taxi Peninsula picks up from Frankston Station 24 hours a day. Book ahead with your train time and the driver will meet you at the pick-up point, or call when you arrive. Sedans suit most trips, and our wheelchair accessible vans and Maxi WAT carry passengers in their chairs. MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi to meet me at Frankston Station late at night?
faq.a: Yes. We run 24 hours a day. Book ahead with your expected arrival time and the driver will be waiting at the pick-up area. If your train is delayed, call us or reply to your confirmation and we will adjust. This is a good way to avoid waiting for a late bus.

faq.q: I’ve missed the Stony Point train. Can you take me instead?
faq.a: Yes. If you have missed your connection at Frankston, we can take you straight to Stony Point, Hastings, Crib Point or anywhere else on the Peninsula. Book online or call us, and the driver will meet you near the station.

name: Southern Cross Station
description: Taxi from Southern Cross Station home to Frankston or the Mornington Peninsula after V/Line, coach or SkyBus trips. Book 24/7 online.
entrance: Southern Cross has step-free access throughout, with lifts and ramps connecting platforms, the concourse and the street.
spot: We meet you at a permitted pick-up point near the station. The driver will confirm the spot by SMS or phone, as the station is large and has several exits.
parking: Stopping near the station is restricted and the surrounding streets are busy. Drivers wait in a legal pick-up spot and call you when they arrive.
access: The station is fully accessible, with lifts and level access. If you are in a wheelchair, book a wheelchair accessible taxi and tell us which exit you are near.
tips: Tell us which service you are arriving on (V/Line, coach or SkyBus) so we can plan the meeting point.
Allow time to walk from your platform to the exit.
Ask for a fixed quote for the trip back to the Peninsula.
If you have lots of luggage, book a larger vehicle.
about: Southern Cross Station on Spencer Street is Melbourne’s main hub for regional and interstate travel. It is the terminus for V/Line regional trains and coaches, interstate trains and coaches, and the SkyBus service from Melbourne Airport, as well as being a major metropolitan station.

Peninsula residents often arrive at Southern Cross after a trip to regional Victoria, an interstate train, or the SkyBus from the airport. From there, getting home to Frankston or further down the Peninsula involves a train change and possibly a bus, which is tiring with luggage, especially late at night. Travellers coming home from the airport on SkyBus often have large suitcases and may have been travelling for many hours. Those returning on V/Line from regional Victoria may arrive late in the evening, when trains to Frankston run less often. A direct taxi saves several transfers and gets you home without carrying bags up and down platforms.

Taxi Peninsula picks up from Southern Cross and takes you straight home. Book ahead with your arrival time, or call when you get in. Our drivers help with bags, and our wheelchair accessible vehicles carry passengers in their chairs. Fixed quotes are available on request for the trip down to the Peninsula.

faq.q: Can you pick me up at Southern Cross after a V/Line trip?
faq.a: Yes. Book ahead with your expected arrival time and we will meet you at a pick-up point near the station. If your train is late, call us or reply to your confirmation. We can then take you straight home to Frankston or anywhere on the Mornington Peninsula.

faq.q: Where should I wait for my taxi at Southern Cross?
faq.a: Southern Cross is large with several exits. When the driver arrives, they will confirm the pick-up spot by SMS or phone. Tell us which exit you are near or which service you arrived on, and the driver will meet you as close as possible.

name: Flinders Street Station
address: Corner Flinders Street and Swanston Street, Melbourne VIC 3000
description: Taxi from Flinders Street Station to Frankston or the Peninsula after a night in the city. Wheelchair taxis available, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: Flinders Street Station has step-free access from the main entrance on the corner of Flinders and Swanston Streets, with lifts and ramps to most platforms.
spot: The driver collects you from a nearby street where taxis are allowed to stop. The driver will confirm the spot by SMS or phone, as streets around the station are busy and stopping is restricted.
parking: Flinders Street and Swanston Street have trams, restricted stopping and heavy foot traffic. The driver will phone you from a nearby spot where stopping is allowed.
access: The station has lifts and ramps to most platforms. If you are in a wheelchair, book a wheelchair accessible taxi and tell us where you are waiting.
tips: The clocks above the main entrance are a well-known meeting point, but the driver may need to meet you nearby where stopping is permitted.
Book ahead after major events, when demand is high.
Request a fixed quote if you would like a set price for the ride home.
Tell us how many are travelling if you are in a group.
about: Flinders Street Station is Melbourne’s best-known landmark station, at the corner of Flinders and Swanston Streets opposite Federation Square. It is the hub of the metropolitan train network and the start of many trips home, including on the Frankston line.

Peninsula residents often head into the city for a show, a sporting event at the MCG or Rod Laver Arena, or a night out. Getting home late can mean a long train ride to Frankston followed by a wait for a bus or a taxi. After a big event, crowds on trains can be heavy. For groups, a single taxi or Maxi WAT can be more convenient and comfortable than several people travelling separately by train and then needing a lift from Frankston. Passengers with wheelchairs or mobility aids also find a direct ride much easier than crowded late-night trains and station changes.

Taxi Peninsula can pick you up from Flinders Street and take you straight home. Book ahead with your expected time and the driver will meet you at a permitted spot nearby. Groups can travel together in our Maxi WAT, and wheelchair users are well catered for. Fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: Can you pick me up after a concert or game in the city?
faq.a: Yes. Book ahead with your expected finish time, or use “pick up when ready” and call us when you are ready. The driver will meet you at a permitted spot near Flinders Street Station. After big events, roads are busy, so allow a little extra time.

faq.q: Can a group of us travel together?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know how many are in your group when you make the booking. Our Maxi WAT carries up to six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, which suits groups heading home together after a night out. A sedan suits smaller groups, and everyone travels straight home without changing trains at Frankston.

name: Stony Point Station
description: Taxi from Stony Point Station to Hastings, Crib Point or anywhere on the Peninsula. Meet the ferry or train, wheelchair taxis available.
entrance: Stony Point Station is a small station at the end of the line, beside the ferry terminal. If you need step-free access, mention it when you book and the driver will meet you at the most suitable point.
spot: We meet you beside the station or near the ferry terminal, depending on where you are coming from. The driver will confirm by SMS or phone.
parking: There is space to stop near the station, and our driver will wait nearby until you are ready.
access: The station is small and quiet, with a short distance from platform to street. If you are travelling with a wheelchair, book a wheelchair accessible taxi.
tips: Trains on the Stony Point line are infrequent, so book ahead if you need to connect with a particular train or ferry.
If you are arriving by ferry, tell us which ferry you are on.
The area is quiet late at night, so book in advance for evening pick-ups.
about: Stony Point Station is the end of the Stony Point line, a diesel shuttle service that runs from Frankston through Baxter, Somerville, Hastings and Crib Point. It sits right next to the Stony Point ferry terminal, where ferries leave for French Island and Phillip Island.

Passengers arriving at Stony Point by train or ferry often need to get somewhere the train does not go, such as Balnarring, Flinders, Red Hill or back up to Mornington. Trains run only every so often, and bus options from Stony Point are very limited, so a taxi is often the most practical choice. Island residents arriving on the ferry for medical appointments in Frankston or beyond often need a direct ride, and visitors returning from a day on French Island may arrive tired and laden with bikes or bags. Locals from Crib Point and nearby areas who do not drive also rely on taxis for trips to Hastings, Frankston or Mornington. Late in the day, when trains are far apart, a booked taxi waiting at the station saves a long wait in a quiet spot.

Taxi Peninsula picks up from Stony Point Station and the ferry terminal at any hour. Book ahead with your arrival time, and we will be there when you arrive. Sedans suit most trips, and our wheelchair accessible vehicles carry passengers in their chairs.

faq.q: Can you meet me at Stony Point when I get off the ferry?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up at Stony Point for the ferry’s arrival time, and the driver will meet you near the terminal or station. If the ferry is delayed, call us or reply to your confirmation. This is particularly useful for evening arrivals, when the area is quiet.

faq.q: Is it easier to get a taxi from Stony Point than wait for a train?
faq.a: Often, yes. The Stony Point line runs infrequently, and the next train may be a long wait. A taxi takes you straight to your destination, anywhere on the Peninsula or further afield. Book ahead or call us when you arrive.

name: Bayside Shopping Centre
description: Taxi from Bayside Shopping Centre in Frankston home with your shopping. Driver helps with bags, wheelchair taxis available, 24/7 bookings.
entrance: Bayside Shopping Centre has several entrances to different parts of the centre. Most are step-free.
spot: We pick you up at the entrance you choose, where stopping is permitted. Tell us which entrance and the driver will confirm by phone.
parking: The centre has its own car parks, and stopping at the entrances is restricted. Drivers wait in a permitted pick-up spot and call you when they arrive.
access: The centre has lifts and step-free paths between levels. Let us know if you need help with shopping bags from the entrance to the taxi.
tips: Tell us which entrance you will be waiting at.
Use “pick up when ready” if you are not sure how long your shopping will take.
The driver will help load your shopping into the boot and carry it to your door.
about: Bayside Shopping Centre is the main shopping centre in central Frankston, close to the train station and the foreshore. It has supermarkets, larger stores, specialty shops and food outlets, and is a regular stop for residents across Frankston and the northern Peninsula.

Many of our passengers use Bayside for their weekly shop, but getting home with heavy bags on the bus is hard work. Older shoppers, people with limited mobility and those without a car find a taxi home the easiest option. Some passengers combine a shopping trip with an appointment in central Frankston, a visit to the library or lunch near the foreshore, and need a ride home at the end of the day. Others have mobility aids or wheelchairs, which makes a crowded bus difficult. Having a driver help carry the bags from the centre to the kitchen bench makes the weekly shop much more manageable.

Taxi Peninsula picks up from Bayside and takes you straight home, with the driver helping load your shopping and carry it to your door. Use “pick up when ready” and call when you have finished, or book a set pick-up time. Wheelchair accessible taxis are available, and we accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts.

faq.q: Can the driver help with my shopping bags?
faq.a: Yes. Our drivers help door to door, including loading your shopping at the centre and carrying it to your front door. Let us know when you book if you have a lot of bags or a shopping trolley, so we can send a suitable vehicle.

faq.q: Can I use my MPTP card for a shopping trip?
faq.a: Yes. If you hold a Multi Purpose Taxi Program card, show it to the driver and the subsidy will be applied to your fare. MPTP can be used for everyday trips like shopping, appointments and social outings, so a regular trip to Bayside for the weekly shop is a good use of it.

name: Karingal Hub
description: Taxi from Karingal Hub in Frankston home with your shopping. Driver helps with bags, wheelchair taxis available, book online 24/7.
entrance: Karingal Hub has several entrances around the centre. Most are step-free, with level access from the car parks.
spot: We pick up at the entrance you name, in a spot where stopping is allowed. The driver will confirm the meeting point by phone or SMS.
parking: The centre has large car parks, and our drivers wait in a permitted area until you are ready.
access: Main entrances have step-free access. Our drivers help with bags from the entrance to the taxi.
tips: Tell us which entrance or which end of the centre you will be waiting at.
If you are staying for a film or a meal, use “pick up when ready” for the trip home.
Ask the driver to help with bags if you have a big shop.
about: Karingal Hub is a large shopping centre on Cranbourne Road in Frankston. It has supermarkets, a range of specialty stores, food outlets and entertainment, and serves Frankston, Karingal, Langwarrin and the surrounding suburbs.

Shoppers who no longer drive, or who simply prefer not to carry heavy bags on the bus, often book a taxi home from Karingal Hub. It is also a popular spot for a film or meal, and many people would rather not drive home afterwards. Residents of Langwarrin, Carrum Downs and the surrounding suburbs also use the centre for banking, health services and everyday errands. For older shoppers, people who use a wheelchair or walker, and anyone without a car, a taxi is the simplest way to get there and back. The driver can help load the shopping into the vehicle and carry it to your front door, which saves a lot of effort, and you can come and go at whatever time suits you, including later in the evening.

Taxi Peninsula collects you from Karingal Hub and takes you home, with the driver helping with your shopping. Book a set time or use “pick up when ready”, and choose a wheelchair accessible vehicle if you need one. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi home after a film at Karingal Hub?
faq.a: Yes. Use “pick up when ready” when you book, then tap “I’m ready” or call us when the film finishes. We run 24 hours, so late sessions are no problem. The driver will meet you at the entrance you choose.

faq.q: Can you take my wheelchair and my shopping?
faq.a: Yes. Book a wheelchair accessible van, which has room for your wheelchair as well as your shopping bags. The driver will secure your chair with four-point restraints and a lap-sash seatbelt, and help load your bags. If you use a heavier power chair, choose the Maxi WAT with its hydraulic hoist.

name: Westfield Southland
description: Taxi from Westfield Southland in Cheltenham to Frankston or the Peninsula. Driver helps with shopping bags, wheelchair taxis, 24/7.
entrance: Westfield Southland has many entrances around the centre, including from car parks and Southland train station. Most are step-free.
spot: We pick you up at a permitted spot near the entrance you name. The centre is large, so tell us which entrance you will be at.
parking: The centre has multi-level car parks, and drivers wait in permitted areas only. The driver will call you when they arrive.
access: The centre has lifts, escalators and step-free paths between levels. Drivers help with bags from the entrance to the vehicle.
tips: Southland is large; name your entrance or the nearest major store when booking.
Use “pick up when ready” so you are not rushing.
Ask for a fixed quote for the trip home to the Peninsula.
about: Westfield Southland is one of Melbourne’s largest shopping centres, on the Nepean Highway in Cheltenham. It has department stores, supermarkets, hundreds of specialty shops, dining and a cinema, and it has its own train station on the Frankston line.

Peninsula residents make the trip to Southland for a bigger range of shops, especially before Christmas or for larger purchases. Getting home with heavy bags or bulky items on the train is hard, and some prefer not to drive in busy traffic. Some Peninsula residents take the train to Southland station and then prefer a taxi home with their purchases. Others visit with a friend or family member who uses a wheelchair, and need a vehicle that can carry both the chair and the shopping. Older shoppers may also prefer not to drive in the busy car parks and on the Nepean Highway. A single booking takes care of the whole trip home.

Taxi Peninsula picks you up from Southland and takes you home to Frankston or the Peninsula. The driver helps load your shopping and carry it to your door. Choose a sedan or a wheelchair accessible vehicle, and ask for a fixed quote for the longer trip.

faq.q: Southland is huge. How will the driver find me?
faq.a: Tell us which entrance you will be waiting at, or the nearest major store. When the driver arrives, they will confirm the exact pick-up spot by SMS or phone. If you are unsure, call us and we will help you find a suitable meeting point.

faq.q: Can you take large purchases?
faq.a: Let us know what you have bought when you book. Small items fit in a sedan boot, but for larger boxes, a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT has more space. The driver will help load and unload your purchases.

name: Rosebud Plaza
description: Taxi from Rosebud Plaza home to Rosebud, Rye, Dromana or Sorrento. Driver helps with shopping bags, wheelchair taxis available, 24/7.
entrance: Rosebud Plaza has entrances from its car parks. Most are step-free.
spot: The driver collects you near your chosen entrance, wherever stopping is allowed. The driver will confirm by phone or SMS.
parking: The centre has a large car park, and our driver will wait in a permitted area until you are ready.
access: Main entrances have step-free access, and our driver can help shoppers with walkers or wheelchairs between the door and the vehicle.
tips: Tell us which entrance you will be at.
In summer, the centre and Rosebud roads are busy, so book ahead.
Use “pick up when ready” for an unhurried shop.
about: Rosebud Plaza is the main shopping centre in Rosebud, serving the southern Mornington Peninsula. It has supermarkets, specialty stores and food outlets, and is a main place for groceries and everyday shopping for residents of Rosebud, Rye, Dromana, Capel Sound and Tootgarook.

Many southern Peninsula residents, particularly older people, do not drive and find the bus home with heavy shopping difficult. In summer, holidaymakers also visit Rosebud Plaza for supplies, and parking can be busy. For residents of Rye, Tootgarook, Capel Sound, McCrae and Dromana, Rosebud Plaza is the nearest large shopping centre, but the trip without a car can involve a long walk to the bus and a wait. Older shoppers with walkers, or people in wheelchairs, find the bus particularly difficult. A taxi takes you from your door to the centre and back, and the driver helps carry the shopping inside, which turns a tiring outing into a simple one.

Taxi Peninsula collects you from Rosebud Plaza and takes you home, with the driver helping with your bags. Book a set time or use “pick up when ready”, and choose a wheelchair accessible vehicle if needed. MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts can all be used.

faq.q: Can I book a regular shopping trip to Rosebud Plaza?
faq.a: Yes. Many passengers book the same trip each week for their shopping. Book online or call us, and use “pick up when ready” for the trip home so you can shop at your own pace. MPTP cards can be used for these trips, and the driver will help carry your bags inside.

faq.q: I’m on holiday in Rye. Can you take me to Rosebud Plaza?
faq.a: Yes. We pick up from holiday houses, rentals and caravan parks right across the southern Peninsula. Give us your full address and any site or unit number, and the driver will take you to the Plaza and back again with your shopping, helping to carry the bags inside when you arrive.
